question: Electrovalent compounds show conduction of electricity in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Molten State**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Electrovalent compounds conduct electricity in molten and aqueous states, but not in solid states:
 
• In the solid state, electrovalent compounds do not conduct electricity because the ions are rigid and cannot move.
 
• However, in the molten state, the electrostatic forces of attraction between the oppositely charged ions weaken, allowing the ions to move freely and conduct electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Kerosene
 
• Kerosene is a liquid fuel that is used in stoves for cooking. It is a substance that has a definite volume but no fixed shape. Kerosene was originally made from coal and oil shale, but later from petroleum. It was the primary commercial use for petroleum refined in the United States until 1909, when motor fuels became more popular. 
 
• Solid state
 
• A solid is a state of matter with a definite shape and volume. Solids form when the energy of atoms decreases and they take up a relatively ordered, three-dimensional structure. 
 
• Petrol
 
• Petrol is a liquid fuel that is used in vehicles. Petrol and kerosene are miscible liquids, meaning they can be mixed together. Fractional distillation is a process that can be used to separate petrol, kerosene, and other components from crude oil.
